title: The Wages of Sin and the Gift of God
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Every sin, even the small ones, brings death, and death is not natural. Jesus took our sin to the grave and left it there.
exhortation: Yesterday we talked about the fact that we are all sinners, every one of us, no exceptions. But why is that such a big deal? Sure, big sins like murder and stealing are bad. But what about a small lie? The answer is yes. Every sin, even the ones we think are small, brings death.

We weren't made to die. Sin brought death. We can pretend it's natural to die after a long, full life, but it isn't. Death is bad any way you look at it. It's so bad that most of the time we don't even think about it, and when we do, we romanticize it to make it less frightening. But death is frightening and unnatural.

Jesus came to defeat death, and he succeeded by his own death, because he had no sin. He took our sin to the grave and rose victorious over death, leaving our sin in the grave forever. Now, for those who trust in him, though we die physically, death is just a doorway to eternal life. That's why Paul says in 1 Corinthians 15, "O death, where is your victory? O death, where is your sting? The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law. But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ."

Do you have reason to fear death this morning? If you aren't a believer, you do. But the good news is that Jesus has made a way to pass from death to life. Today is the day to humble yourself and receive the forgiveness and salvation found only in Jesus, the risen Savior, who loves us and conquered death for all who believe in him.
prayer: Lord, thank you for calling us out of darkness and into your light. Help us bring our sin into the light without shame, where once it's exposed it can shrivel up and die.
In the face of such mercy, kindness and grace, we can bring all of it to you without shame, knowing that you have completed the work. Thank you, Jesus.
